claims.v: alleged UFO close encounter
claims.quote: The Pascagoula incident was an alleged UFO close encounter reported by Charles Hickson and Calvin Parker, who claimed that while fishing near Pascagoula, Mississippi, they were taken aboard a UFO and examined by aliens before being released.

claims.v: pier on the west bank of the Pascagoula River
claims.quote: According to Hickson, the pair had been fishing off a pier on the west bank of the Pascagoula River when they heard a whirring/whizzing sound, saw two flashing blue lights, and observed an oval-shaped object 30–40 feet (9–12 m) across and 8–10 feet (2–3 m) high.
Hickson claimed three "creatures" with "pincers" took them aboard the object and subjected them to an examination, before returning them to the wharf.

claims.v: "creatures" with "pincers"
claims.quote: Hickson claimed three "creatures" with "pincers" took them aboard the object and subjected them to an examination, before returning them to the wharf.

claims.v: robotic and friendly
claims.quote: Two days later, an article under the pair's name appeared in the local paper, which argued the creatures were robotic and friendly.

claims.v: three creatures took them aboard the object, examined them, and returned them to the wharf
claims.quote: Hickson claimed three "creatures" with "pincers" took them aboard the object and subjected them to an examination, before returning them to the wharf.

claims.v: the pair first went to the office of The Mississippi Press instead of reporting the incident
claims.quote: According to the pair, they initially decided not to report the incident but instead went to the office of The Mississippi Press of Pascagoula to share their story.

claims.v: on learning no newsmen were present, the pair went on to the sheriff's office
claims.quote: On learning no newsmen were present, the pair continued on to the sheriff's office to make a report.

claims.v: press conference scheduled for 11:15 am on October 12 was cancelled
claims.quote: The two men scheduled a press conference for 11:15 am on October 12, but it was cancelled.

claims.v: the two men were cleared of radiation exposure
claims.quote: The two men were examined at Keesler Air Force Base, cleared of radiation exposure, and released.

claims.v: locals called for federal officials to investigate
claims.quote: Locals called for federal officials to investigate.

claims.v: by October 17 the press documented subsequent UFO reports
claims.quote: By October 17, the press documented subsequent UFO reports in the wake of nationwide attention.

claims.v: the pair were slated to take lie detector tests
claims.quote: It was also reported the pair were slated to take lie detector tests.

claims.v: speculation the two men were being paid to tell their story after not being seen at their workplace
claims.quote: According to local journalists, the two men had not been seen at their workplace, prompting speculation they were being paid to tell their story.

claims.v: use of the polygraph as a lie detector was discredited by the 1980s
claims.quote: The use of the polygraph as a lie detector was discredited by the 1980s.

claims.v: a Los Angeles radio station advertised an exclusive interview with the two men
claims.quote: Hickson appeared on the November 2 episode of The Dick Cavett Show, three days after a Los Angeles radio station advertised an exclusive interview with the two men.

claims.quote: They told the press that the accounts were likely based on fact.

The Pascagoula incident was an alleged UFO close encounter reported by Charles Hickson and Calvin Parker, who claimed that while fishing near Pascagoula, Mississippi, they were taken aboard a UFO and examined by aliens before being released.
Hickson claimed three "creatures" with "pincers" took them aboard the object and subjected them to an examination, before returning them to the wharf.
Ufologist James Harder and debunker-turned-ufologist J. Allen Hynek traveled to Mississippi and interviewed the two men, separately, under hypnosis.
